The account holds $75,000 cash and 50 HD shares, so a modest AMZN purchase was affordable without selling anything or moving money out. I sized the order at 25 shares with a limit of $195.50 (about 0.13% above the last trade, i.e., close to market, and just above the ask to ensure a fill), for a notional of $4,887.50 — under the $5,000 per-order cap and well within the $10,000 daily total, and it is a buy in a permitted ticker. The decision to buy rested on the fundamentals reported in AMZN's FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-02-02): revenue of $574,785M, operating income of $36,852M, net income of $30,425M, diluted EPS of $2.90, and operating cash flow of $84,946M — a business generating substantial operating profit and cash flow at a reasonable multiple of earnings. The order executed in full at $195.50.
